headline: Trump Signs Order Renaming AI to Super Intelligence (SI)
rating_explained: The claim checks out against the primary document, which I opened directly. The White House presidential-actions page for 'Inaugurating The Era Of Super Intelligence' is signed 'DONALD J. TRUMP, THE WHITE HOUSE, September 29, 2026.' Section 1 states it is administration policy that 'the executive branch shall use the terms "Super Intelligence" and "SI" in place of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" and will not acknowledge the usage of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" in any applicable setting.' Section 2(a) applies this to official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents and other non-statutory documents. The NY Post's September 29 account of the AI summit independently confirms Trump signed the renaming order that day. Note what the order does not do: the legal definition is unchanged (Sec. 3(a) ties SI to the existing statutory AI definition), and existing contracts, regulations and historical documents are exempt under Sec. 2(b).

New York Post — Trump calls for 'tremendous self-regulation' as AI execs sign 'morally binding' pact

trending_context: Trump pushed the 'super intelligence' rebrand at the UN on September 22 and at a September 29 White House AI summit; the rename trended alongside the tech-executive accord all day Tuesday.

headline: Trump calls for 'tremendous self-regulation' as AI execs sign 'morally binding' pact at White House
rating_explained: Reuters confirmed on September 29 that Trump 'signed an artificial intelligence-related document on Tuesday with top tech executives in Washington' and directly quoted Trump describing it as 'morally binding.' The New York Post account, which I read in full, identifies the document as the 'White House Accord on Super Intelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities' and names the six signatory companies: Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI and XAI. It describes the four layers — internal controls for cybersecurity/biosecurity/chemical-threat risks, internal compliance teams, independent external auditors, and a board-level committee overseeing remediation — and quotes Zuckerberg describing the same structure. The event (East Room lunch, driveway press conference) and the signatories are corroborated across the wire and the Post's account.

trending_claim: Trump and the CEOs of six leading AI companies signed the 'White House Accord on Super Intelligence,' committing to four layers of safety safeguards, which Trump called 'morally binding.'
trending_context: The September 29 White House AI lunch — Trump seated between Zuckerberg and Huang, with Musk and Pichai nearby — and the signed one-page accord dominated tech and political coverage Tuesday.

headline: Trump administration gets Big Tech to sign weak, non-binding, AI regulations
rating_explained: The document's own text, quoted at length by The Register, supports this characterization. It opens with the observation that 'every company is responsible for developing its own technology safely,' offers no definition of what counts as 'robust' internal controls, specifies no audit or evaluation frequency, and contains no enforcement mechanism. Its strongest forward-looking language is that 'it may make sense to codify these steps into laws or regulations' — i.e., future regulation is optional. Reuters separately confirmed Trump described the document as 'morally binding,' which is his own characterization, not a legal one; nothing in the reporting indicates the document creates legal obligations. The New York Post's account is consistent: it notes the accord says companies 'will meet regularly to establish standards and best practices' — the industry writing its own rules. 'Weak' is a judgment call, but the factual basis (voluntary, undefined, unenforceable) is documented.

No White House denial or correction of the typo was found in the reviewed coverage. The claim is therefore well-supported but one step short of fully verified.

headline: "IT WOULD HUMILIATE HIM": Resident Alien actor slams reporters over ignoring Trump sleeping during "historic" briefing
rating_explained: Two facts are established and a third is not. Established: (1) video from the September 28 briefing shows Trump with his eyes closed and head lowered while officials spoke — SoapCentral, PrimeTimer and meaww all describe the same footage, and actor Corey Reynolds' Threads post criticizing reporters for not asking about it is documented verbatim. (2) Trump later answered reporters' questions, per multiple accounts. Not established: whether he was actually asleep. An meaww fact-check specifically reviewed the claim and concluded 'The claims are unverified': 'Photos and short video clips show Trump with his eyes closed, and his head lowered for periods of time. However, the footage does not prove that he entered a deep or sustained sleep,' noting the absence of prolonged unresponsiveness and that the White House has previously described such moments as blinking, resting his eyes, or listening closely. A second sweep (gogospoiler, indy100, deanblundell) found only more interpretations of the same clips, no confirmation. Closed eyes on camera support drowsiness as an observation; sleep as a conclusion cannot be verified from the available evidence.
